security_spec.violation_condition: In the Linux kernel, when TRAP_ON_UNIMPLEMENTED_INSTRUCTION is false in the hardware implementation and misa.A is cleared (e.g., by firmware or a hypervisor that does allow A-disabling), any subsequent kernel execution of Zaamo/Zabha AMO instructions (e.g., amoswap used in atomic primitives) enters 'unpredictable' hardware state instead of raising IllegalInstruction. The kernel assumes AMO instructions either execute atomically or trap — it has no code path to handle silent non-atomic execution.
security_spec.summary: Spec now allows AMO instructions to enter unpredictable state (not just trap) when misa.A=0 on implementations with TRAP_ON_UNIMPLEMENTED_INSTRUCTION=false, breaking the kernel invariant that AMOs either execute atomically or trap — KVM currently blocks misa.A writes but non-KVM hypervisors or firmware could trigger silent atomicity loss
